# RFC-0001: Strider: streaming and out-of-core point cloud processing

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @wael
> **Tags:** `architecture`, `out-of-core`, `licensing`, `performance`

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-INTRO] Introduction (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-intro"></a>

**Strider** is a Rust library ecosystem and a Qt6 desktop workbench for processing point clouds that do
not fit in memory. It reads a terabyte-scale cloud — from a local file or over HTTP — renders it,
classifies it, edits it and writes results, without ever materialising the whole dataset. The name is the
premise: you *stride over* terrain rather than sink into it.

It is two things deliberately, and the split matters to anyone reading further. The libraries are
permissively licensed and meant to be adopted by other tools; the application is the finished product.
C-LICENSE specifies the boundary and why it falls where it does.

#### The system

Five components, layered so that each is usable without the ones above it:

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| **spatial access** | traverses a source's spatial index and answers "give me this volume at this level of detail" as a stream of Arrow batches; owns the node cache |
| **format adapters** | COPC, LAS/LAZ, Parquet/GeoParquet, E57 — none privileged in the internal model |
| **operators** | one processing step each: crop, reproject, estimate normals, classify ground. Each *declares* what it needs from its input |
| **renderer** | draws the viewport; see [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md) for what it takes from its host and what it may depend on |
| **application** | the Qt6 workbench, and the host that supplies every capability the libraries are denied |

Between them sits a **planner** whose entire job is satisfying what operators declare — inserting
repartitioning, halo construction and summary passes so that a neighbourhood algorithm gets the
neighbours it needs. That planner is the reason this specification exists, and [RFC-0002:C-EXEC](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-exec) is its contract.

#### Where to start

Not exhaustive — who tends to need each, where the titles alone would not say.

- **RFC-0001** (this document) — what Strider is, who may use it, and what a release may claim.
- **[RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md)** — if you intend to write an operator, or want to know what the engine guarantees.
- **[RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md)** — before trusting a number you intend to deliver to someone else.
- **[RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md)** — if you are embedding a library crate, targeting an unusual environment, or looking for
  where caching lives.
- **[RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md)** — if your data spans coordinate systems, or if heights matter to your result.
- **[RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md)** — if you are integrating the renderer, or deciding what may be drawn over a viewport.
- **[RFC-0007](../rfc/RFC-0007.md)** — if you are building editing tools, or need to know what record is kept of a change.

Vocabulary is defined once in `CONTEXT.md` and not redefined here. The *why* behind each substantive choice
lives in the accompanying architecture decisions, which these clauses point to rather than restate.



### [RFC-0001:C-MOTIVATION] Motivation and prior art (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-motivation"></a>

Strider exists because of one gap, and the gap is narrow enough to state precisely: **no tool
processes point cloud neighbourhoods out of core.** Streaming and processing are each solved; their
intersection is not.

A neighbourhood algorithm — normal estimation, statistical outlier removal, cloth-simulation ground
filtering, segmentation — needs points beyond whatever partition it is handed, because a point at the
edge of a partition has neighbours in the next one. Every existing tool resolves that by holding the
whole cloud, or by not offering the algorithm.

#### The landscape

| Tool | Streams a large cloud | Processes | Neighbourhoods out of core |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CloudCompare | ✗ | ✓ rich | ✗ — reads COPC but decompresses it whole and builds an in-memory octree, so the format's hierarchy buys nothing |
| QGIS | ✓ local and remote | ✗ | ✗ — an excellent viewer; since 3.42 it edits point attributes, but in place, only on a local COPC, and never positions |
| PDAL | ✓ genuinely streaming | ✓ CLI pipelines | ✗ — see below |
| Potree | ✓ billions of points | ✗ | ✗ — visualisation only |
| Entwine | ✓ | indexing only | ✗ |
| FUSION | ✓ | ✓ forestry-focused | partial — out of core for many operations, but a forestry toolset rather than a general workbench |

PDAL is the closest and the most instructive. Its stages declare whether they can stream, and the
neighbourhood ones cannot: `filters.normal` takes a whole point view and does not inherit the
streamable interface, and `filters.outlier` documents two passes over the full view to compute global
statistics. So PDAL streams a crop and classifies ground from a raster, then holds everything in
memory the moment a k-nearest-neighbour query appears. That boundary is a property of its
architecture rather than an omission, which is why it has not simply been fixed.

#### The claim

Strider's differentiating claim is therefore singular and testable: **a neighbourhood operator
evaluated over a partitioned dataset produces the same result as the same operator evaluated over the
whole dataset, in memory that does not grow with the dataset.** Everything expensive in this
specification — requirement declaration, a planner obliged to satisfy them, halo supply, and the
prohibition on treating an overlapping partitioning as disjoint — exists to make that one sentence
true. C-CONFORMANCE is how it is demonstrated rather than asserted.

Two secondary claims follow from the same machinery: a delivered result is reproducible bit for bit,
and a result that diverges from its whole-dataset equivalent says so.

#### What Strider is not

It is not a faster CloudCompare, and not a graphical front end for PDAL. It shares PDAL's streaming
premise and CloudCompare's interactive ambition, and the reason those have not previously combined is
architectural rather than a matter of effort — that reasoning is recorded in the architecture
decisions accompanying this RFC, not restated here.

The primary domain is forestry LiDAR, and nothing in the specification presumes it: the vocabulary is
domain-neutral and COPC is one source adapter among several, so bathymetry, urban survey and
industrial scanning are additions rather than reshapings.

### [RFC-0001:C-OVERVIEW] Overview and scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-overview"></a>

This document is the front door: what Strider is, why it exists, who may use it, and what a release of it is
entitled to claim. The technical contracts live in the six RFCs that follow.

**Scope** — who may use Strider and on what terms, including contribution; and what a release must verify
before asserting a property of itself.

**Out of scope** — every technical obligation. The operator contract is [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md); evaluation guarantees
[RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md); environment capabilities and caching [RFC-0004](../rfc/RFC-0004.md); coordinates and point references
[RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md); rendering [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md); editing [RFC-0007](../rfc/RFC-0007.md). Also out of scope: trademark policy, packaging,
release process, and which milestone ships what — a plan rather than an obligation.

Licensing and conformance are grouped here because both are policy a reader needs before trusting anything
the software says. Licensing decides who may build on this; conformance decides what the project may assert.
Both also fail in the same way — invisibly, until it is expensive. A copyleft dependency beneath a permissive
crate makes that crate's declared licence false while everything still builds; bounded memory, halo
correctness and reproducibility each hold on every dataset a developer has to hand and fail in production. So
both are written as checks rather than intentions.

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0001:C-LICENSE] Licence assignment, declaration and dependency compatibility (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-license"></a>

The libraries are permissive so the ecosystem can adopt them; the application is copyleft so it
cannot be repackaged proprietarily. The boundary is the **crate**, which is also the unit a
dependency-licence check can verify.

1. Every published library crate MUST be licensed `Apache-2.0 OR MIT` and MUST declare exactly
   that expression in its package manifest. A library crate MUST NOT be published under a copyleft
   licence.
2. Every distributed application, including any future network-accessible service, MUST be
   licensed `AGPL-3.0-or-later`.
3. Licensing MUST be machine-readable across the whole repository, per the REUSE specification:
   - every authored source file MUST carry inline `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` and
     `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers;
   - files that do not take comment headers cleanly MUST be bulk-annotated in `REUSE.toml`;
   - the full text of every licence in use MUST be present under `LICENSES/`.
4. A library crate MUST NOT depend, directly or transitively, on a component whose licence imposes
   obligations beyond `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`.
   - Compliance MUST be verified automatically against the resolved dependency graph, not by review alone.
   - Verification MUST run on every dependency change.
   - A library crate MUST NOT depend on a component whose permissive availability rests on a commercial
     licence held by this project.
   - This constrains library crates only. The application MAY depend on copyleft components,
     including Qt under its open-source terms, consistent with (2).

#### Rationale

The dual expression in (1) is not stylistic: `Apache-2.0` alone is incompatible with **GPL-2.0-only**, so MIT
is what keeps the crates usable by such a consumer, and Apache is what supplies a patent grant. Which
ecosystem that adoption is aimed at, and why copyleft libraries would forfeit it, is a comparative question
argued in the accompanying architecture decision.

AGPL rather than GPL in (2) costs nothing on the desktop, where the network clause never fires, and covers a
hosted component without a second licence.

(4) is required because a copyleft dependency beneath a library crate makes that crate's declared licence
false while everything still builds — the declaration in (1) becomes a misrepresentation, and it surfaces
only when an adopter's lawyer reads the tree. Transitive reach is the substantive part; a directly-added
dependency gets scrutiny, one arriving three levels down by a minor version bump does not. Hence automatic
verification on every dependency change rather than at review.

The third sub-item generalises past Qt deliberately. A dual-licensed dependency can always be argued
compliant *for this project*, and the argument is always wrong for adopters.

### [RFC-0001:C-CONTRIB] Contribution terms and relicensing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-contrib"></a>

Contribution terms determine what the project can later do with its own code. The choice here deliberately
forecloses one class of business model in exchange for lower contribution friction, and that trade is stated
rather than left to be discovered.

1. Contributions MUST be accepted under the same licence as the artefact contributed to.
   - A separate copyright assignment MUST NOT be required.
   - A contributor licence agreement MUST NOT be required.
2. The project MUST NOT represent that it can relicense contributed code.
   - It MUST NOT offer proprietary relicensing of any artefact containing contributions accepted under (1).
3. The inbound terms MUST be stated in the repository, where a contributor encounters them before
   contributing.

#### Rationale

(2) states a consequence rather than leaving it to be discovered: holding no assignable copyright means the
project cannot relicense, so **open-core and sell-exceptions models are foreclosed**. Why that trade is worth
making is argued in the accompanying architecture decision, along with what it costs.

(3) is what makes (1) a term rather than an assumption. Terms a contributor never saw are not terms they
accepted, and this is the only obligation here visible from outside the project.

### [RFC-0001:C-CONFORMANCE] Release claims (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-conformance"></a>

Every claim this project makes will be believed true before it is verified, and stated publicly on that
belief, at which point correcting it is embarrassing rather than routine. This clause makes the claim
contingent on the check instead of on confidence.

1. A release MUST NOT assert a property whose corresponding verification has not passed.
   - Where a property is verified only under stated conditions, those conditions MUST be published with the
     assertion.
   - Where a definition in `CONTEXT.md` and a normative clause disagree, the clause governs.
   - The verifications themselves live with the properties they establish: bounded memory at
     [RFC-0002:C-MEMORY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-memory) 5, halo correctness at [RFC-0002:C-HALO](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-halo) 4, halo removal without rewriting at
     [RFC-0002:C-HALO](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-halo) 6, single materialisation at [RFC-0002:C-MATERIALISATION](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-materialisation) 4, reproducibility
     at
     [RFC-0003:C-COMMIT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-commit) 6, reduction determinism across configurations at [RFC-0003:C-COMMIT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-commit) 9,
     projection transparency at [RFC-0002:C-PROJECTION](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-projection) 3, and operator conformance at
     [RFC-0002:C-VERIFIED](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-verified).

#### Rationale

The obligation is deliberately about *assertion* rather than about achievement. Nothing here requires a
release to have any particular property; it requires that whatever it claims has been checked. That is the
only form of the rule this document can own, because every property it would otherwise describe belongs to
another RFC.

A young project satisfies this more easily than it appears, because every honesty obligation in the
specification has a **refusal half** implementable before its capability half. Mismatched coordinate systems
and vertical references are refused ([RFC-0005:C-TRANSFORM](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-transform) 4, [RFC-0005:C-VERTICAL](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-vertical) 1); unsatisfiable
pipelines are rejected naming the unmet requirement ([RFC-0002:C-EXEC](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-exec) 2). Refusal is what those clauses
prescribe, so "transformation is not implemented yet" is a conformant position rather than an unmet
obligation — a release may be honest without being complete.
